Hi Alex / team — attaching the items you requested. Summary below and attachments are redacted where appropriate.

Quick summary (technical):
- Retention model: tenant-scoped logs live in S3 buckets with per-tenant prefixes; runtime ephemeral logs are also buffered in node-local storage and streamed to object storage within 5–15 minutes. Retention TTLs are implemented as lifecycle policies and a daily background sweep.
- Erasure workflow (two modes):
  1) Automatic TTL deletion: objects past TTL are removed by lifecycle policy + verification job (md5 mismatch checks + tombstone marker)
  2) Customer-scoped erasure exception: when a customer requests a targeted delete prior to TTL (or requests proof-of-delete), we trigger the manual erasure pipeline: a ticket is created in our audit queue, the tenant prefix is snapshotted, deletion jobs run against object storage and KV caches, and an event (proof_of_delete) is emitted and signed by our internal key (HSM-backed) with an event id.
- Audit trail: every manual exception includes a ticket id, operator id, time, list of object prefixes removed, and a signed event (example attached: proof_of_delete_event_9832.log).

Attachments included:
- redacted_log_export.json (sample listing of tenant objects prior to deletion; names redacted)
- proof_of_delete_event_9832.log (signed event with redacted signatures; contains ticket id: RDW-9832)
- retention_playbook_v2.pdf (two-page runbook, sections: scope, operator steps, verification checks)

Notes & caveats:
- For Nimbus-specific exceptions that derive from legal hold, we will keep a read-only snapshot in a privileged escrow for the hold duration — that’s a manual step and will be documented in the SOW if requested.
- We redact PII from the sample artifacts; full artifacts require an NDA amendment or a secured artifact exchange (we can use a signed, time-limited Drive link).

If you want a certified digest (SHA256) of the deleted objects list we can produce that as an additional signed artifact.

-Jonas

--
Jonas Weber
